% P:meth-platforms
Table~\ref{tab:params} lists both platforms. The mobile platform pairs the Snapdragon 8 Gen 3~\cite{sd8g3} host and
NPU with PIM on LP-Spec's~\cite{lpspec} LPDDR5-6400. The NPU computes at its measured FP16 GEMM rate~\cite{hao2025},
used for INT8\ASSUMPTION, and reads the memory at the bandwidth of Section~\ref{sec:bg:roofline}. Each host visit costs
30\,\textmu s of NPU dispatch~\cite{npufaster}\ASSUMPTION; the host draws 2.285\,W while busy,
the Snapdragon 8 Gen 3's~\cite{sd8g3} decode power net of its DRAM~\cite{hao2025,heterollm,tman}\ASSUMPTION. The edge server pairs
P3-LLM's~\cite{p3llm} NPU, priced at its peak rate\ASSUMPTION, with one HBM2 stack; the NPU idles at 55\,W, the chip idle power of TPUv4i~\cite{tpuv4i},
while the PIM works\ASSUMPTION.

\subsection{PIM Designs and Area}
\label{sec:method:designs}
% P:meth-designs-area
Each substrate carries four designs, stock AiM~\cite{aimjssc}, P3-LLM-style, LP-Spec-style and CoDe, with one
controller and the platform's PU placement (Table~\ref{tab:params}). Every design computes at its
platform's precision (Section~\ref{sec:bg:cmd}), with a 4-bit KV cache on HBM2, and every design's arithmetic is
priced as INT4\,$\times$\,INT8 integers\ASSUMPTION. On the
mobile platform CoDe's tile of $V = 8$ spans two column periods, so one MAC command serves eight tokens. On HBM2 each
token's staging slice is twice as large and every PU serves two banks, so CoDe uses $V = D = 4$
there; Section~\ref{sec:eval:ablation} sizes $V$ on both platforms. CoDe reaches LP-Spec-style's peak on
the mobile platform with 0.539$\times$ its logic area per die: arithmetic takes 0.73 of LP-Spec-style's logic and 0.34
of CoDe's, while storage, the staging queue, accumulator file and weight latch, takes 0.32 of CoDe's logic and 0.10
of LP-Spec-style's. On HBM2, CoDe's logic is 0.56$\times$ LP-Spec-style's and 1.33$\times$ P3-LLM-style's, an area
that buys twice P3-LLM-style's beats per column.

\subsection{Simulator and Models}
% figure* (Section VI-A): placement checked on the float map after each build
\begin{figure*}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figs/fig_gemm.pdf}
  \caption{GEMMs against $M$, mobile platform (top) and edge server (bottom): (a)~speed-up over stock AiM;
  (b)~GOPS per logic mm$^2$.}
  \label{fig:gemm}
\end{figure*}

% P:meth-simulator
We extend the open-source trace-driven AiM simulator, built on Ramulator~2.0~\cite{ramulator2} and used by
CENT~\cite{cent}, with each design's commands and a PU model that holds a MAC command until the PU has finished the
beats of the previous command; every PIM kernel runs at cycle level. Our P3-LLM-style model reproduces
P3-LLM's~\cite{p3llm} own step gain of depth 2 over a depth-1 PIM: 1.78$\times$ at INT8 against the 1.6$\times$ P3-LLM
reports. On the mobile platform the simulator gives P3-LLM-style's per-token commands no separate C/A slot;
re-timed on the C/A bus, the commands lower P3-LLM-style's $U$ from 0.355 to 0.351, and on the edge server the
simulator times them. On the mobile platform the simulator issues an all-bank refresh every $t_\mathrm{REFI}$ and blocks every command to
the rank for $t_\mathrm{RFCab}$, the JEDEC values of a 16\,Gb die (Table~\ref{tab:params}), which we assume for our
dies\ASSUMPTION;
refresh then takes $\rho = 0.070$ of stock AiM's time at $M = 1$ (Section~\ref{sec:bg:cmd}). Area comes from synthesis of each PU's lanes and registers in a 45\,nm library, scaled to a 1z DRAM process by
the estimated area of AttAcc's~\cite{attacc} GEMV unit in that process; the GB is priced as DRAM-process
SRAM\ASSUMPTION. PU power and energy come from synthesis of each design's whole PU with Yosys and ABC~\cite{abc} on the
Nangate45 library, OpenROAD~\cite{openroad} placement and clock-tree synthesis, and OpenSTA power from a zero-delay
simulation with random operands. We scale the synthesised energy to the DRAM process so that an AiM-style bf16 PU from
the same flow spends the compute share of CENT's~\cite{cent} AiM MAC-command energy, and with the square of the voltage
to the 1.05\,V supply (VDD2H on LPDDR5); leakage scales the same way\ASSUMPTION. Peak power runs every PU at its full
MAC rate and includes leakage, GB reads and the column fetch, which adds 87.6\,mW per die on the mobile platform and
54.8\,mW per pseudo-channel on HBM2 to every design. Energy per token charges each issued MAC its PU's synthesised energy,
leakage over the step time, GB reads priced by SRAM size~\cite{horowitz}, and CENT's~\cite{cent} per-command DRAM
energies. In every design a PU's clock runs only on its MAC beats, so an idle PU cycle costs leakage
only\ASSUMPTION.

\subsection{Algorithms and Workloads}
\label{sec:method:work}
% P:meth-workloads
The mobile platform runs speculative decoding of Llama-2-7B in INT8 with a 1.1B-parameter draft model: $M - 1$
drafted tokens and one verify pass of $M$ rows, acceptance rate 0.7 per token and context $L = 1024$. The ablation of Section~\ref{sec:eval:ablation} also drafts with
an EAGLE~\cite{eagle} head. The edge server runs batched decoding of
Llama-2-7B and 13B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B and Mistral-7B at a 4K context, one token per request per step. End to
end, every system runs the mobile loop at $M = 4$ and the edge server's batch at $M = 8$. NPU only runs the whole model
on the NPU; in NPU + $X$, PIM design $X$ runs every weight GEMM and attention layer and the NPU runs the element-wise
work. GEMMs use six FC shapes of Llama-2-7B and Llama-3.2-1B on the mobile platform and the 25 FC shapes of the five
models on the edge server.

\subsection{Metrics}
% P:meth-metrics
GEMM speed counts a GEMM's operations over its time including the drain of its output sums, relative to stock AiM;
end-to-end speed is tokens per second, relative to NPU only. Area efficiency divides
either throughput by the PIM logic area over all dies or pseudo-channels of Table~\ref{tab:params}. Energy is system
energy per token. Edge-server values are geometric means over the five models.
